questions.prompt: A CUDA kernel elects one leader per warp with (threadIdx.x & 31) == 0. On a 64-wide wavefront, what happens?
options: Two leaders per wavefront: anything the leader does per warp is done twice

questions.prompt: Why did Volta break code that relied on implicit warp-synchronous execution?
options: Independent thread scheduling: lanes of a warp may no longer move in lockstep without explicit _sync operations
questions.explanation: That's why the _sync intrinsics take a mask.

questions.prompt: What does hipify do, and what doesn't it do?
options: It translates CUDA API names to HIP mechanically, but doesn't fix hard-coded warp-size assumptions or retune performance
It runs CUDA binaries on AMD

questions.prompt: Which usually need retuning when moving a fast kernel to another vendor's GPU?
options: The mathematical definition of the operation
questions.explanation: The math stays; the mapping changes.

questions.prompt: Why is "many targets, one programming model" good news for GPU compiler engineers?
options: Someone has to build and tune the backends and the tile-level compilers that map one model onto many machines
It reduces the need for testing
